families.name: Package & build
families.blurb: Package managers, version managers, build tools and task runners.

families.name: Containers & clusters
families.blurb: Container runtimes, Compose, local Kubernetes and image builders.

families.name: Inner loop
families.blurb: Live-update loops, process runners, Kubernetes dev tools and cluster bridges.

families.name: Dev environments
families.blurb: Reproducible shells, dev containers and cloud workspaces.

families.name: Monorepos & frameworks
families.blurb: Monorepo tools, app frameworks with a local story and scaffolders.

families.name: Local services & data
families.blurb: Cloud emulators, local backends, mocks, tunnels, ORMs and migrations.

families.name: AI & agents
families.blurb: Agent frameworks, MCP and agent tools, coding agents, local models and LLM observability.

families.name: Platform
families.blurb: Infrastructure as code, developer portals, CI/CD, GitOps, observability and secrets.

dx.title: Easy to use?
dx.explain: Is the tool easy for you, every day? Each check is 10 points. More checks: more to the right.

criteria.label: One command starts it
criteria.help: A single command brings up the whole thing it manages.

criteria.label: Little setup
criteria.help: Useful out of the box, or with a short generated config.

criteria.label: See changes fast
criteria.help: Live reload, file sync or incremental rebuilds in seconds.

criteria.label: Clear errors
criteria.help: Says what broke and how to fix it, or ships a doctor-style check.

criteria.label: Has a screen to look at
criteria.help: A web dashboard, TUI or desktop app, not only raw logs.

criteria.label: Working in 10 minutes
criteria.help: Official docs get a newcomer to a working result in about ten minutes.

criteria.label: Mac, Linux and Windows
criteria.help: Supported on all three, natively or through WSL.

criteria.label: No account needed
criteria.help: Runs on your machine without signing up or a network round trip.

criteria.label: Light and fast
criteria.help: Starts in seconds and does not need a large VM or many GB of RAM.

criteria.label: AI can drive it
criteria.help: An MCP server, a JSON output mode or an API an AI agent can drive.

parity.title: Made for big, real systems?
parity.explain: Small and simple: one service, nothing around it. Big and real: many services, real databases, containers, Kubernetes, the cloud, logs, big teams. Each check is 10 points. More checks: higher up.

criteria.label: Works with containers
criteria.help: Runs, builds or watches containers.

criteria.label: Handles many services
criteria.help: Brings up, connects or watches several services together.

criteria.label: Services talk to each other
criteria.help: Service-to-service networking, DNS or ingress like production.

criteria.label: Real databases and queues
criteria.help: Databases, queues or volumes, not only in-memory fakes.

criteria.label: Same images as live servers
criteria.help: Uses the images, bundles or lockfiles that production uses.

criteria.label: Speaks Kubernetes
criteria.help: Manifests, pods, Helm charts or a real Kubernetes API.

criteria.label: Works with the cloud
criteria.help: Emulates or reaches real cloud provider APIs.

criteria.label: Real config and secrets
criteria.help: Environment, config and secrets handled the way production handles them.

criteria.label: Logs, metrics, traces
criteria.help: Exposes telemetry the way production does.

criteria.label: Works for big teams
criteria.help: Built for many services and many developers sharing a setup.

rings.label: Adopt
rings.help: Use it. Stable, updated in the last 6 months, lots of people use it.

rings.label: Trial
rings.help: Try it. Still young (before 1.0), or quiet for 6 to 18 months, or few users yet.

rings.label: Assess
rings.help: Watch it. Brand new, less than a year old.

rings.label: Hold
rings.help: Avoid for now. Dead, deprecated, or no update in 18 months.

agents.name: LangGraph
agents.tagline: Stateful graphs for LLM agents
agents.note: Durable checkpoints need a store such as Postgres; the local dev server UI pairs with paid LangSmith.

agents.name: LangChain
agents.tagline: Model, tool and retriever building blocks for LLM apps
agents.note: Many layers of abstraction; the 1.0 rewrite moved agent runtime onto LangGraph.

agents.name: CrewAI
agents.tagline: Role-based multi-agent crews and flows in Python
agents.note: Telemetry is on by default; set CREWAI_DISABLE_TELEMETRY to opt out.

agents.name: AutoGen
agents.tagline: Microsoft's multi-agent conversation framework
agents.note: In maintenance mode; Microsoft points new work to Microsoft Agent Framework. Last release Sep 2025.

agents.name: AG2
agents.tagline: Community fork of AutoGen 0.2 for multi-agent apps
agents.note: Shares AutoGen's history but not its current API; check which one a tutorial targets.

agents.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
agents.tagline: Successor to Semantic Kernel and AutoGen for .NET and Python
agents.note: Python and .NET packages version separately; many samples assume Azure AI Foundry.

agents.name: Semantic Kernel
agents.tagline: Microsoft SDK for AI plugins in C#, Python and Java
agents.note: Still released, but Microsoft positions Agent Framework as the place for new agent work.

agents.name: Mastra
agents.tagline: TypeScript framework for agents, workflows and RAG
agents.note: Some packages, such as the auth and cloud pieces, are under a source-available license rather than Apache-2.0.

agents.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
agents.tagline: Lightweight agents, handoffs and guardrails from OpenAI
agents.note: Still 0.x. Tracing goes to the OpenAI dashboard by default unless you swap the processor.

agents.name: Claude Agent SDK
agents.tagline: The Claude Code agent loop as a library
agents.note: Still 0.x; wraps the Claude Code CLI, so it needs Node and an Anthropic account or cloud provider.

agents.name: Google ADK
agents.tagline: Google's Agent Development Kit for Python, Java, Go and TS
agents.note: Model-agnostic in theory, but deployment docs lean heavily on Vertex AI and Cloud Run.

agents.name: Pydantic AI
agents.tagline: Type-safe Python agent framework from the Pydantic team
agents.note: Durable execution comes from integrations such as Temporal or DBOS, not the core.

agents.name: LlamaIndex
agents.tagline: Data and retrieval framework for LLM agents
agents.note: Still 0.x after years; integrations are split into hundreds of separately versioned packages.

agents.name: Haystack
agents.tagline: Pipelines for RAG and agents from deepset

agents.name: DSPy
agents.tagline: Program and optimize LM pipelines instead of prompting
agents.note: Optimizers can make many paid model calls; budget before running them.

agents.name: Vercel AI SDK
agents.tagline: TypeScript toolkit for LLM apps, streaming UI and agents
agents.note: Major versions have broken APIs roughly yearly; pin the major and read the migration guide.

agents.name: smolagents
agents.tagline: Hugging Face's minimal code-writing agents
agents.note: Code agents execute generated Python; use the Docker or E2B executor, not the local one, for untrusted tasks.

agents.name: Agno
agents.tagline: Python agents and teams with a runtime and control plane
agents.note: The hosted control-plane UI needs an Agno account; the framework itself runs locally.

agents.name: Letta
agents.tagline: Stateful agents with long-term memory, formerly MemGPT
agents.note: Pre-1.0 server; the self-hosted path is a Docker image backed by Postgres.

agents.name: Temporal
agents.tagline: Durable execution for long-running agent workflows
agents.note: The local dev server is one binary; production self-hosting is a real distributed system.

agents.name: Inngest
agents.tagline: Durable steps, queues and AgentKit for serverless code
agents.note: The server is source-available (SSPL with delayed Apache); the SDKs are Apache-2.0.

agents.name: Restate
agents.tagline: Durable execution engine for agents and services
agents.note: Server is under the Business Source License; SDKs are MIT.

agents.name: Model Context Protocol
agents.tagline: Open protocol and SDKs connecting agents to tools and data
agents.note: Spec revisions are dated; check which revision each client and SDK implements.

agents.name: MCP Inspector
agents.tagline: Visual test and debug tool for MCP servers

agents.name: Docker MCP Toolkit
agents.tagline: Run catalog MCP servers as containers behind one gateway
agents.note: The gateway is open source; the toolkit UI ships in Docker Desktop, which is paid for larger companies.

agents.name: Smithery
agents.tagline: Registry and hosting for MCP servers
agents.note: Acquired by Arcade in 2026; hosted connections are reported to shut down Oct 2026, the registry stays.

agents.name: MCP Registry
agents.tagline: Official community registry of public MCP servers
agents.note: A metadata index for clients and sub-registries, not a place to browse or install servers by hand.

agents.name: FastMCP
agents.tagline: Pythonic framework for MCP servers and clients
agents.note: Major versions moved fast (v2 to v4 in about a year); pin the major.

agents.name: Composio
agents.tagline: Hosted tool integrations and auth for agents
agents.note: Tool calls and OAuth tokens run through Composio's cloud; there is no fully local mode.

agents.name: skills.sh
agents.tagline: Directory and CLI for installing agent skills
agents.note: Skills are third-party instructions and scripts; read them before installing.

agents.name: Stagehand
agents.tagline: Browser automation SDK for agents, by Browserbase
agents.note: Runs a local browser for free; Browserbase's hosted browsers are the paid path.

agents.name: Playwright MCP
agents.tagline: MCP server that drives a browser through Playwright
agents.note: Still 0.0.x versioning; accessibility snapshots can use many tokens on large pages.

agents.name: E2B
agents.tagline: Cloud sandboxes for running agent-generated code
agents.note: SDKs and infra code are open source, but the practical path is the hosted service with an API key.

agents.name: Claude Code
agents.tagline: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for the terminal and IDEs
agents.note: Closed source despite the public repo; needs a Claude subscription or API billing.

agents.name: Codex
agents.tagline: OpenAI's coding agent for terminal, IDE and cloud
agents.note: The CLI is Apache-2.0 but still 0.x; using it needs a ChatGPT plan or OpenAI API key.

agents.name: Cursor
agents.tagline: AI-first code editor forked from VS Code
agents.note: Requires an account; code context is sent to Cursor's servers even with your own API key.

agents.name: Gemini CLI
agents.tagline: Google's open-source terminal agent for Gemini
agents.note: Still 0.x with weekly releases; free-tier quotas and model routing change often.

agents.name: GitHub Copilot
agents.tagline: GitHub's AI pair programmer, agent mode and cloud agent
agents.note: Premium-request quotas govern the stronger models and agent features.

agents.name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
agents.tagline: Cognition's agentic IDE, renamed from Windsurf
agents.note: Renamed in 2026 after Cognition bought Windsurf; plans and features are still being merged with Devin.

agents.name: Cline
agents.tagline: Open-source coding agent for VS Code and the terminal
agents.note: Bring your own model key; costs track your provider's token billing directly.

agents.name: Roo Code
agents.tagline: VS Code agent forked from Cline, now discontinued
agents.note: Repo archived May 2026; the team moved to a cloud product. Cline is the suggested migration path.

agents.name: Aider
agents.tagline: Git-aware AI pair programming in the terminal
agents.note: No tagged release since Aug 2025; still pre-1.0. Re-check before relying on it.

agents.name: Continue
agents.tagline: Open-source IDE agent and CI checks with any model
agents.note: Works fully local with Ollama or LM Studio; the hub and shared configs need an account.

agents.name: Zed
agents.tagline: Fast Rust editor with built-in agent panel and ACP
agents.note: Hosted AI features need a Zed account; external agents plug in through the Agent Client Protocol.

agents.name: Warp
agents.tagline: Agentic terminal and development environment
agents.note: The client is now AGPL on GitHub, but AI features are metered and need a Warp account.

agents.name: Amp
agents.tagline: Coding agent for terminal and editors, from Sourcegraph
agents.note: No versioned releases and features change weekly; threads are stored on Amp's servers.

agents.name: OpenCode
agents.tagline: Open-source terminal coding agent for any model
agents.note: Repo moved from sst/opencode to anomalyco/opencode; old install links may redirect.

agents.name: goose
agents.tagline: Local, extensible open-source AI agent built on MCP
agents.note: Moved from Block to the Agentic AI Foundation; repo and docs URLs changed in 2026.

agents.name: Kiro
agents.tagline: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE and CLI
agents.note: Requires sign-in through AWS Builder ID or a social login; usage is credit-metered.

agents.name: Jules
agents.tagline: Google's asynchronous cloud coding agent
agents.note: Runs in Google-hosted VMs against GitHub repos only; nothing runs on your machine.

agents.name: Devin
agents.tagline: Cognition's autonomous cloud software engineer
agents.note: Runs in Cognition's cloud workspaces; pricing is per compute unit.

agents.name: Paradev (formerly Superset)
agents.tagline: Desktop app to run many coding agents in parallel worktrees
agents.note: Renamed from Superset in 2026; source-available (ELv2). Orchestrates agents like Claude Code, is not one.

agents.name: Conductor
agents.tagline: Mac app to run parallel Claude Code and Codex agents
agents.note: macOS only; uses your own Claude or Codex subscription for the agents it runs.

agents.name: Ollama
agents.tagline: Run open models locally behind a simple API
agents.note: Widely used but still 0.x by version; the desktop app and cloud models are additions to the OSS server.

agents.name: LM Studio
agents.tagline: Desktop app to download and serve local models
agents.note: The app is closed source; the lms CLI and SDKs are MIT. Pre-1.0 versioning.

agents.name: llama.cpp
agents.tagline: C/C++ inference for GGUF models on CPU and GPU
agents.note: Ships many builds a day with pre-1.0 versions; pin a build for reproducible results.

agents.name: vLLM
agents.tagline: High-throughput LLM serving engine
agents.note: Built for Linux GPU servers; macOS and Windows support is limited. Still 0.x.

agents.name: LocalAI
agents.tagline: Self-hosted OpenAI-compatible API for many model types
agents.note: Container images are large because they bundle several inference backends.

agents.name: Docker Model Runner
agents.tagline: Pull and run models as OCI artifacts with Docker
agents.note: Easiest through Docker Desktop, which is paid for larger companies; Docker Engine works on Linux.

agents.name: Jan
agents.tagline: Open-source desktop ChatGPT alternative that runs offline
agents.note: Pre-1.0; aimed at chat use more than serving models to other apps.

agents.name: MLX LM
agents.tagline: Run and fine-tune LLMs on Apple silicon with MLX
agents.note: Apple silicon Macs only; pre-1.0.

agents.name: Langfuse
agents.tagline: Open-source LLM tracing, evals and prompt management
agents.note: Self-hosting v3 and later needs Postgres, ClickHouse, Redis and S3-compatible storage.

agents.name: LangSmith
agents.tagline: LangChain's tracing, evals and deployment platform
agents.note: Hosted SaaS; self-hosting is an Enterprise-plan feature.

agents.name: Arize Phoenix
agents.tagline: Open-source LLM tracing and evaluation on OpenTelemetry
agents.note: Source-available under the Elastic License 2.0, not an OSI license.

agents.name: Helicone
agents.tagline: Proxy-based LLM logging and AI gateway
agents.note: Team joined Mintlify in Mar 2026; reported to be in maintenance mode, last tagged release Aug 2025.

agents.name: OpenLLMetry
agents.tagline: OpenTelemetry instrumentation for LLM libraries
agents.note: Pre-1.0; GenAI semantic conventions in OpenTelemetry are still changing underneath it.

agents.name: Braintrust
agents.tagline: Evals, logging and prompt playground for AI products
agents.note: The platform is closed SaaS; only the SDKs are open source.

agents.name: promptfoo
agents.tagline: CLI for LLM evals and red teaming in CI
agents.note: Acquired by OpenAI in Mar 2026; the CLI stays MIT and multi-provider so far. Still 0.x.

agents.name: Opik
agents.tagline: Open-source LLM tracing and evals from Comet
agents.note: Self-hosting runs several containers, including ClickHouse and MySQL.

containers.name: Docker Engine
containers.tagline: The open-source Docker daemon and CLI for Linux
containers.note: Linux only; macOS and Windows need a VM such as Docker Desktop, OrbStack or Colima.

containers.name: Docker Desktop
containers.tagline: Docker Engine, Compose and Kubernetes in a desktop app
containers.note: Paid subscription required for larger companies; the VM reserves several GB of RAM.

containers.name: Podman
containers.tagline: Daemonless, rootless container engine
containers.note: Mostly Docker CLI compatible, but rootless networking and some Compose files behave differently.

containers.name: Podman Desktop
containers.tagline: Desktop app for Podman, Kubernetes and other engines
containers.note: Electron app on top of a Podman machine VM, so memory use is similar to Docker Desktop.

containers.name: Rancher Desktop
containers.tagline: Desktop containers and k3s Kubernetes, free and open
containers.note: Heavier than Colima or OrbStack; switching between moby and containerd resets images.

containers.name: OrbStack
containers.tagline: Fast, light Docker and Linux VMs for macOS
containers.note: macOS only and closed source; commercial use needs a paid licence.

containers.name: Colima
containers.tagline: Minimal container runtimes on macOS and Linux via Lima
containers.note: Pre-1.0; file sharing and VM networking are slower than OrbStack, and no Windows.

containers.name: Lima
containers.tagline: Linux VMs with containerd for macOS and Linux
containers.note: A VM building block; most people use it through Colima, Rancher Desktop or Finch.

containers.name: containerd
containers.tagline: Industry-standard container runtime daemon
containers.note: Low-level runtime with no friendly CLI of its own; pair it with nerdctl or Kubernetes.

containers.name: nerdctl
containers.tagline: Docker-compatible CLI for containerd
containers.note: Linux native; on macOS it runs inside Lima. Compose support covers most but not all fields.

containers.name: Finch
containers.tagline: AWS's open-source client for container development
containers.note: Smaller community than Docker or Podman; no built-in Kubernetes.

containers.name: Apple container
containers.tagline: Run Linux containers as light VMs on Apple silicon
containers.note: Pre-1.0, Apple silicon and recent macOS only; no Compose and limited networking between containers.

containers.name: Docker Compose
containers.tagline: Define and run multi-container apps from YAML
containers.note: No Kubernetes semantics; Compose files drift from cluster manifests unless kept in sync.

containers.name: Compose Watch
containers.tagline: File sync and rebuild-on-change for Docker Compose
containers.note: Sync works only for paths in the build context; large trees and bind mounts can be slow on macOS.

containers.name: Podman Compose
containers.tagline: Run Compose files with Podman
containers.note: Covers less of the Compose spec than Docker Compose; podman compose can also call docker-compose.

containers.name: Kompose
containers.tagline: Convert Compose files to Kubernetes manifests
containers.note: Output is a starting point; generated manifests usually need hand edits for probes and storage.

containers.name: kind
containers.tagline: Kubernetes clusters in Docker containers
containers.note: Still 0.x; built for testing Kubernetes, so ingress and LoadBalancer need extra setup.

containers.name: k3d
containers.tagline: Run k3s clusters in Docker
containers.note: Inherits k3s differences from upstream, such as Traefik and SQLite by default.

containers.name: k3s
containers.tagline: Lightweight certified Kubernetes distribution
containers.note: Linux only; on macOS or Windows run it through k3d, Rancher Desktop or a VM.

containers.name: minikube
containers.tagline: Local Kubernetes for learning and development
containers.note: Heavier than kind or k3d, especially with VM drivers; start-up takes a minute or more.

containers.name: MicroK8s
containers.tagline: Canonical's low-ops Kubernetes with add-ons
containers.note: Installed as a snap on Linux; macOS and Windows go through a Multipass VM.

containers.name: k0s
containers.tagline: Single-binary, zero-dependency Kubernetes
containers.note: Aimed at servers and edge; for laptop dev on macOS it needs a VM or k0s in Docker.

containers.name: vcluster
containers.tagline: Virtual Kubernetes clusters inside a host cluster
containers.note: Needs a host cluster to run in; some features sit in the paid vCluster Platform.

containers.name: Kubernetes
containers.tagline: Upstream container orchestration, as a reference point
containers.note: Not a local dev tool on its own; you reach it locally through kind, k3d, minikube and friends.

containers.name: BuildKit / buildx
containers.tagline: Docker's concurrent, cache-efficient image builder
containers.note: Remote and multi-platform caching needs registry or cache backend setup to pay off.

containers.name: Cloud Native Buildpacks
containers.tagline: Build OCI images from source without a Dockerfile
containers.note: pack is still 0.x; builder images are large and first builds are slow.

containers.name: ko
containers.tagline: Build Go container images without Docker
containers.note: Go only, pre-1.0; no Dockerfile means no system packages without a custom base image.

containers.name: Jib
containers.tagline: Daemonless container images for Java via Maven or Gradle
containers.note: JVM only, and release activity has slowed; check recent releases before adopting.

containers.name: Kaniko
containers.tagline: Build images from a Dockerfile inside Kubernetes
containers.note: Google archived it in June 2025; Chainguard maintains a security-patch fork (chainguard-forks/kaniko).

containers.name: Buildah
containers.tagline: Build OCI images without a daemon
containers.note: Linux only; on macOS and Windows it runs inside a Podman machine.

containers.name: Nixpacks
containers.tagline: Build images from source using Nix packages
containers.note: In maintenance mode and not under active development; Railway recommends Railpack.

containers.name: Railpack
containers.tagline: Zero-config image builder on BuildKit, from Railway
containers.note: Pre-1.0 and still labelled beta by some platforms; language coverage is narrower than Nixpacks had.

containers.name: Depot
containers.tagline: Hosted remote BuildKit builders with shared cache
containers.note: Builds run on Depot's servers, so it needs an account and network access.

containers.name: Portainer
containers.tagline: Web UI for Docker, Podman and Kubernetes
containers.note: Community Edition is open source; RBAC and other team features need the paid Business Edition.

containers.name: Lazydocker
containers.tagline: Terminal UI for Docker and Compose
containers.note: Pre-1.0 and releases are infrequent; Docker API only, so Podman needs the Docker socket shim.

containers.name: Dive
containers.tagline: Explore image layers and find wasted space
containers.note: Pre-1.0 with long gaps between releases; an image inspector, not a runtime manager.

environments.name: Nix
environments.tagline: Purely functional package manager and dev shells
environments.note: Steep learning curve; the Nix language and flakes take real time to learn.

environments.name: devenv
environments.tagline: Nix-based dev environments with services and processes
environments.note: Requires Nix underneath; first evaluation can be slow.

environments.name: Devbox
environments.tagline: Isolated shells from Nix packages without writing Nix
environments.note: Still 0.x; installs Nix for you, which is the source of most errors.

environments.name: Flox
environments.tagline: Nix-backed environments you can share and layer
environments.note: Sharing environments through FloxHub needs an account.

environments.name: direnv
environments.tagline: Loads and unloads env vars per directory
environments.note: Only manages environment variables; pair it with Nix, devenv or a version manager.

environments.name: Distrobox
environments.tagline: Any Linux distro in a container, integrated with the host
environments.note: Linux only. Shares your home directory, so it is not an isolation boundary. Last release April 2026.

environments.name: Toolbx
environments.tagline: Container-based mutable shells for Fedora and RHEL
environments.note: Linux only and best supported on Fedora; still 0.x, last release September 2025.

environments.name: Dev Containers
environments.tagline: Open spec and CLI for container-based dev environments
environments.note: The spec and CLI are open source; the VS Code extension that provides the UI is not.

environments.name: DevPod
environments.tagline: Client-only dev containers on any backend
environments.note: No release since March 2025. A community fork continues as Devsy (devsy.sh).

environments.name: Vagrant
environments.tagline: Reproducible VM-based dev environments
environments.note: Business Source License since 2023. Full VMs are heavy. Last release August 2025.

environments.name: GitHub Codespaces
environments.tagline: Hosted dev containers attached to GitHub repos
environments.note: Billed per core-hour beyond the free quota; GitHub-hosted repositories only.

environments.name: Ona
environments.tagline: Cloud environments and AI agents, formerly Gitpod
environments.note: Gitpod renamed to Ona in 2025 and refocused on AI agents; Gitpod Classic was shut down.

environments.name: Coder
environments.tagline: Self-hosted remote workspaces defined in Terraform
environments.note: You run and operate the control plane; some governance features are in the paid edition.

environments.name: Eclipse Che
environments.tagline: Kubernetes-native browser IDE workspaces
environments.note: Needs a Kubernetes or OpenShift cluster to host it; heavy to operate for a small team.

environments.name: code-server
environments.tagline: VS Code in the browser on any machine you run
environments.note: An editor only; uses the Open VSX registry, so some Microsoft extensions are missing.

environments.name: Daytona
environments.tagline: Former dev-environment manager, now AI code sandboxes
environments.note: Pivoted from dev environments to sandboxes for AI-generated code; the GitHub repo was archived in 2026.

environments.name: CodeSandbox
environments.tagline: Browser sandboxes and microVM dev environments
environments.note: Acquired by Together AI in 2024; product focus has been shifting toward AI sandboxes.

environments.name: StackBlitz
environments.tagline: Node.js dev environments running in the browser tab
environments.note: WebContainers run Node only; no Docker, native binaries or real databases.

environments.name: Replit
environments.tagline: Hosted IDE with built-in hosting and an AI agent
environments.note: Your code runs and deploys on Replit's platform; hard to mirror a non-Replit production setup.

environments.name: Google Cloud Workstations
environments.tagline: Managed dev environments inside your Google Cloud project
environments.note: Google Cloud only, billed per hour plus a cluster management fee.

environments.name: Firebase Studio
environments.tagline: Sunsetting browser workspace from Google, formerly IDX
environments.note: New workspaces disabled since June 2026; full shutdown planned for March 2027.

environments.name: AWS Cloud9
environments.tagline: Browser IDE on EC2, closed to new customers
environments.note: No longer available to new customers since July 2024; AWS points to IDE toolkits and CloudShell.

environments.name: Microsoft Dev Box
environments.tagline: Cloud Windows workstations for developers
environments.note: Closed to new customers since November 2025; features are moving into Windows 365.

environments.name: DDEV
environments.tagline: Docker-based local stacks for PHP and Node projects
environments.note: Opinionated toward PHP CMS projects; other stacks need custom add-ons.

environments.name: Lando
environments.tagline: Recipe-based Docker dev environments
environments.note: Startup is slower than DDEV on large projects; the v4 rewrite has been in progress for years.

environments.name: Laravel Sail
environments.tagline: Docker Compose setup for Laravel apps
environments.note: Laravel only; a thin wrapper over Docker Compose.

environments.name: Laravel Herd
environments.tagline: Native PHP and Node dev environment for Laravel
environments.note: macOS and Windows only. Databases, queues and mail capture need Herd Pro.

environments.name: Local
environments.tagline: Desktop app for local WordPress sites
environments.note: WordPress only. Closed source, made by WP Engine; some features push toward its hosting.

environments.name: Docksal
environments.tagline: Docker-based stacks for Drupal and PHP
environments.note: No release since May 2024; most users have moved to DDEV.

foundations.name: npm
foundations.tagline: The package manager bundled with Node.js
foundations.note: Slower installs and a larger node_modules than pnpm or Bun; registry install scripts run by default.

foundations.name: pnpm
foundations.tagline: Fast, disk-efficient Node package manager
foundations.note: Strict node_modules layout can break packages that rely on hoisting.

foundations.name: Yarn
foundations.tagline: Node package manager with workspaces and Plug'n'Play
foundations.note: Classic (v1) and modern (v2+) behave very differently; Plug'n'Play needs editor SDK setup.

foundations.name: Bun
foundations.tagline: JavaScript runtime, package manager and bundler in one
foundations.note: Node API compatibility is high but not complete; check native addons before switching runtime.

foundations.name: Deno
foundations.tagline: JavaScript and TypeScript runtime with built-in tooling
foundations.note: npm compatibility is good since 2.0, but some packages still assume Node-only APIs.

foundations.name: uv
foundations.tagline: Fast Python package and project manager
foundations.note: Still 0.x with frequent releases; pin the uv version in CI. Trial only by the pre-1.0 rule.

foundations.name: pip
foundations.tagline: The standard Python package installer
foundations.note: No lockfile or environment management on its own; pair with venv and a pinned requirements file.

foundations.name: Poetry
foundations.tagline: Python dependency management and packaging
foundations.note: Dependency resolution is noticeably slower than uv on large projects.

foundations.name: PDM
foundations.tagline: Standards-based Python package and project manager
foundations.note: Smaller community than Poetry or uv, so fewer guides and CI examples.

foundations.name: Hatch
foundations.tagline: Python project manager with environments and builds
foundations.note: No lockfile of its own; reproducible installs need an extra tool.

foundations.name: Pipenv
foundations.tagline: Python virtualenv and Pipfile.lock manager
foundations.note: Locking is slow on large dependency sets; most new projects pick uv or Poetry instead.

foundations.name: Rye
foundations.tagline: Experimental Python project manager, superseded by uv
foundations.note: Deprecated by its maintainers in favour of uv; migrate rather than adopt.

foundations.name: Conda
foundations.tagline: Cross-language package and environment manager
foundations.note: Anaconda's default channel has commercial licence terms; use conda-forge for unrestricted use.

foundations.name: Pixi
foundations.tagline: Fast conda and PyPI project manager with lockfiles
foundations.note: Pre-1.0 and moving fast; manifest fields still change between releases.

foundations.name: Cargo
foundations.tagline: Rust's package manager and build tool
foundations.note: Incremental rebuilds of large workspaces are still slow compared with interpreted languages.

foundations.name: Go modules
foundations.tagline: Go's built-in dependency management
foundations.note: Private modules need GOPRIVATE and proxy settings that trip up first-time setups.

foundations.name: Maven
foundations.tagline: Convention-based Java build and dependency tool
foundations.note: Verbose XML and slow cold builds; the JVM start-up makes small edits feel heavy.

foundations.name: Gradle
foundations.tagline: Build automation and dependency tool for the JVM
foundations.note: The daemon uses a lot of RAM, and build logic in Groovy or Kotlin DSL can grow hard to debug.

foundations.name: Composer
foundations.tagline: Dependency manager for PHP

foundations.name: Bundler
foundations.tagline: Gem dependency manager for Ruby
foundations.note: Native extension gems often need system libraries, which is where most install failures come from.

foundations.name: NuGet
foundations.tagline: Package manager for .NET
foundations.note: Lockfiles are opt-in (RestorePackagesWithLockFile), so many repos restore floating versions.

foundations.name: Homebrew
foundations.tagline: Package manager for macOS and Linux
foundations.note: Not for Windows, and formulae float to latest, so it does not pin team tool versions.

foundations.name: Swift Package Manager
foundations.tagline: Swift's built-in package and build manager
foundations.note: Windows and Linux support work, but most of the ecosystem still assumes Apple platforms and Xcode.

foundations.name: mise
foundations.tagline: Polyglot tool versions, env vars and tasks
foundations.note: Releases land very often and calver tags make it easy to drift; pin the version in CI.

foundations.name: asdf
foundations.tagline: Plugin-based version manager for many runtimes
foundations.note: The 0.16 Go rewrite changed commands; plugins are community-maintained and vary in quality.

foundations.name: nvm
foundations.tagline: Shell script to manage Node.js versions
foundations.note: POSIX shells only (Windows needs the separate nvm-windows), and it slows shell start-up.

foundations.name: fnm
foundations.tagline: Fast Node.js version manager written in Rust
foundations.note: Node only; needs a shell hook for automatic switching on cd.

foundations.name: Volta
foundations.tagline: JavaScript tool manager pinned via package.json
foundations.note: Maintainers declared it unmaintained in late 2025 and recommend migrating to mise.

foundations.name: pyenv
foundations.tagline: Install and switch between Python versions
foundations.note: Builds Python from source, so installs are slow and fail without build dependencies; Windows needs pyenv-win.

foundations.name: rbenv
foundations.tagline: Lightweight Ruby version manager
foundations.note: Needs ruby-build to install versions, and no native Windows support.

foundations.name: rustup
foundations.tagline: The Rust toolchain installer

foundations.name: SDKMAN!
foundations.tagline: Manage parallel JDK and JVM tool versions
foundations.note: Bash-based; Windows only through WSL or Git Bash, and the candidate list needs network access.

foundations.name: proto
foundations.tagline: Pluggable multi-language version manager
foundations.note: Pre-1.0 and its WASM plugin ecosystem is much smaller than mise or asdf.

foundations.name: Vite
foundations.tagline: Frontend dev server and build tool
foundations.note: Dev serves unbundled ESM, so dev and production output can still differ in edge cases.

foundations.name: esbuild
foundations.tagline: Extremely fast JavaScript bundler and minifier
foundations.note: Still 0.x by design and minor releases may break; pin it. No type checking.

foundations.name: Rspack
foundations.tagline: Rust bundler compatible with the webpack API
foundations.note: Most webpack loaders work, but not every webpack plugin does.

foundations.name: Rolldown
foundations.tagline: Rust bundler with a Rollup-compatible API
foundations.note: 1.0 shipped in May 2026; watch mode and some optimisations are still marked experimental.

foundations.name: Turbopack
foundations.tagline: Incremental Rust bundler built into Next.js
foundations.note: Only usable through Next.js; webpack plugins and custom configs do not carry over.

foundations.name: webpack
foundations.tagline: Configurable module bundler for JavaScript
foundations.note: Slow on large apps and config-heavy; new projects usually start on Vite or Rspack.

foundations.name: Rollup
foundations.tagline: ES module bundler for libraries
foundations.note: Vite 8 moved to Rolldown, so Rollup's main role is now library builds.

foundations.name: Parcel
foundations.tagline: Zero-configuration web application bundler
foundations.note: Release pace has slowed and its ecosystem is small next to Vite.

foundations.name: SWC
foundations.tagline: Rust compiler for JavaScript and TypeScript
foundations.note: A compiler, not a bundler; most people use it through Next.js, Rspack or Vite plugins.

foundations.name: tsdown
foundations.tagline: Library bundler for TypeScript, powered by Rolldown
foundations.note: Successor to tsup, which is no longer maintained; requires a recent Node.js.

foundations.name: Bazel
foundations.tagline: Hermetic, multi-language build system from Google
foundations.note: Steep learning curve and heavy setup; pays off mainly for very large monorepos.

foundations.name: Buck2
foundations.tagline: Meta's fast multi-language build system
foundations.note: No semver releases and a thin open-source prelude; expect to write your own rules.

foundations.name: Pants
foundations.tagline: Monorepo build system for Python, Go, JVM and more
foundations.note: macOS and Linux only; Windows needs WSL.

foundations.name: Earthly
foundations.tagline: Containerized builds from Dockerfile-like Earthfiles
foundations.note: Upstream says it is no longer actively maintained and cloud features are gone; a community fork is EarthBuild.

foundations.name: Dagger
foundations.tagline: Programmable CI/CD pipelines that run in containers
foundations.note: Pre-1.0 with API changes between releases; needs a running container engine.

foundations.name: Make
foundations.tagline: The classic dependency-based build and task tool
foundations.note: Stable and everywhere; hold only because GNU Make's last release (4.4.1) was Feb 2023. Tabs and shell quirks bite.

foundations.name: Just
foundations.tagline: A command runner with make-like recipes
foundations.note: A command runner, not a build system; no file-based up-to-date checks.

foundations.name: Task
foundations.tagline: YAML-based task runner and build tool in Go
foundations.note: Shell commands run through a Go shell interpreter, so some Bash-isms behave differently.

frameworks.name: Nx
frameworks.tagline: Monorepo build system with task graph and caching
frameworks.note: Remote caching and distributed runs go through Nx Cloud, which is paid beyond a free tier.

frameworks.name: Turborepo
frameworks.tagline: Task runner and cache for JavaScript monorepos

frameworks.name: Lerna
frameworks.tagline: Versioning and publishing for JavaScript monorepos
frameworks.note: Maintained by the Nx team; task running is delegated to Nx under the hood.

frameworks.name: Rush
frameworks.tagline: Microsoft's monorepo manager for large JS repos
frameworks.note: Strict and opinionated; setup takes longer than Turborepo or Nx.

frameworks.name: moon
frameworks.tagline: Rust monorepo task runner with toolchain management

frameworks.name: Lage
frameworks.tagline: Task runner for JS monorepos from Microsoft
frameworks.note: Far smaller community than Nx or Turborepo; mostly used in Microsoft-style repos.

frameworks.name: Changesets
frameworks.tagline: Versioning and changelogs for multi-package repos
frameworks.note: Release management only; it does not run builds or start services.

frameworks.name: Aspire
frameworks.tagline: Code-first app host with dashboard for distributed apps
frameworks.note: Formerly .NET Aspire; the app host is .NET-first even though it can run other languages.

frameworks.name: Encore
frameworks.tagline: Backend framework that provisions infra from code
frameworks.note: Go and TypeScript only; Encore Cloud deployment is a paid product.

frameworks.name: Dapr
frameworks.tagline: Sidecar runtime APIs for distributed applications
frameworks.note: Local self-hosted mode needs Docker and a dapr init step; many concepts to learn.

frameworks.name: Wasp
frameworks.tagline: Full-stack React and Node framework with a DSL
frameworks.note: Still pre-1.0 with breaking changes between minor versions; Windows only through WSL.

frameworks.name: RedwoodJS
frameworks.tagline: Full-stack React, GraphQL and Prisma framework
frameworks.note: In maintenance mode, renamed Redwood GraphQL; no release since Oct 2025, team moved to RedwoodSDK.

frameworks.name: Nitric
frameworks.tagline: Cloud framework with infrastructure inferred from code
frameworks.note: Stable 1.x and actively released, but a small community, so not widely used.

frameworks.name: Quarkus
frameworks.tagline: Java framework with dev mode, Dev UI and Dev Services

frameworks.name: Spring Boot
frameworks.tagline: Java framework with Compose support and devtools

frameworks.name: Micronaut
frameworks.tagline: JVM framework with Test Resources for local deps

frameworks.name: Ruby on Rails
frameworks.tagline: Full-stack Ruby web framework
frameworks.note: Windows support is through WSL.

frameworks.name: Laravel
frameworks.tagline: PHP web framework with Sail for local Docker

frameworks.name: Django
frameworks.tagline: Batteries-included Python web framework
frameworks.note: No built-in story for containers or service dependencies; bring your own Compose.

frameworks.name: Next.js
frameworks.tagline: React framework for full-stack web apps
frameworks.note: Some features behave differently outside Vercel's hosting.

frameworks.name: React Router
frameworks.tagline: React framework mode, successor to Remix

frameworks.name: Astro
frameworks.tagline: Content-first web framework with islands

frameworks.name: NestJS
frameworks.tagline: Structured Node.js framework for server apps

frameworks.name: Hono
frameworks.tagline: Small web framework for any JavaScript runtime

frameworks.name: FastAPI
frameworks.tagline: Python API framework with type-driven validation
frameworks.note: Still versioned 0.x, though long-standing and widely used.

frameworks.name: SST
frameworks.tagline: Infra-as-code framework with live AWS dev mode
frameworks.note: sst dev deploys real resources to your cloud account; there is no fully offline mode.

frameworks.name: Serverless Framework
frameworks.tagline: Deploy and develop AWS Lambda apps from YAML
frameworks.note: v4 requires login and a paid subscription for organizations above $2M annual revenue.

frameworks.name: AWS SAM
frameworks.tagline: AWS CLI to build and run Lambda apps locally
frameworks.note: Local mode emulates Lambda and API Gateway only; other AWS services stay remote.

frameworks.name: Architect
frameworks.tagline: Serverless AWS apps with a local sandbox
frameworks.note: Actively released but a small community; sandbox DynamoDB is an in-memory emulation.

frameworks.name: Wrangler
frameworks.tagline: Cloudflare Workers CLI with local workerd dev

frameworks.name: Vercel CLI
frameworks.tagline: Deploy and emulate Vercel projects locally
frameworks.note: Needs a Vercel account; vercel dev is a partial emulation of the hosted platform.

frameworks.name: Netlify CLI
frameworks.tagline: Run Netlify sites and functions locally
frameworks.note: Most features need a linked Netlify site and account.

frameworks.name: Azure Functions Core Tools
frameworks.tagline: Run and debug Azure Functions locally
frameworks.note: Storage triggers need Azurite or a real storage account running alongside.

frameworks.name: create-t3-app
frameworks.tagline: Scaffold a typesafe Next.js, tRPC and Prisma app
frameworks.note: No release since Nov 2025, so not Adopt by the rubric even though it is widely used.

frameworks.name: create-vite
frameworks.tagline: Official Vite project templates

frameworks.name: Yeoman
frameworks.tagline: Generator ecosystem for scaffolding projects
frameworks.note: Many community generators are unmaintained; check a generator's age before using it.

frameworks.name: JHipster
frameworks.tagline: Generate Spring Boot apps with Angular, React or Vue
frameworks.note: Generated projects are large and opinionated.

frameworks.name: Cookiecutter
frameworks.tagline: Project templates from Jinja-templated directories
frameworks.note: Last release Mar 2026; cannot update a project from its template, unlike Copier.

frameworks.name: Copier
frameworks.tagline: Project templates that can update generated projects

frameworks.name: Plop
frameworks.tagline: Micro-generator for files inside an existing repo
frameworks.note: Last release Jan 2026; stable but slow-moving.

inner-loop.name: Flisk
inner-loop.tagline: Local dev loop for microservices and multi-agent stacks
inner-loop.note: First released October 2026. Local only by design, no Kubernetes manifests. Runs on Docker and Tilt.

inner-loop.name: Tilt
inner-loop.tagline: Live-update loop for multi-service apps
inner-loop.note: Kubernetes mode needs a local cluster; Compose mode is lighter. Tiltfiles are Starlark code.

inner-loop.name: Skaffold
inner-loop.tagline: Build, push and deploy loop for Kubernetes apps
inner-loop.note: Kubernetes only; no built-in UI, feedback comes through the terminal.

inner-loop.name: Garden
inner-loop.tagline: Graph-based build, deploy and test for Kubernetes
inner-loop.note: Still 0.x and the last release was February 2026. Remote build cache needs Garden's hosted service.

inner-loop.name: DevSpace
inner-loop.tagline: File sync and dev mode for Kubernetes workloads
inner-loop.note: Last release April 2026, just outside the six-month adopt window.

inner-loop.name: Okteto
inner-loop.tagline: Dev environments and file sync on a Kubernetes cluster
inner-loop.note: The CLI is open source, but most workflows target the commercial Okteto platform on a remote cluster.

inner-loop.name: Project Tye
inner-loop.tagline: Experimental .NET multi-service runner
inner-loop.note: Archived by Microsoft in 2023; .NET Aspire is the suggested successor.

inner-loop.name: Draft
inner-loop.tagline: Generates Dockerfiles, manifests and pipelines for AKS
inner-loop.note: Still 0.x. A scaffolder, not a live loop; output leans toward Azure Kubernetes Service.

inner-loop.name: werf
inner-loop.tagline: Git-driven build and deploy CLI built on Helm
inner-loop.note: Closer to CI/CD than an inner loop; needs a registry and a cluster.

inner-loop.name: Helm
inner-loop.tagline: Package manager and templating for Kubernetes
inner-loop.note: Go-template charts get hard to read; Helm 4 changed some plugin and SDK behavior.

inner-loop.name: Kustomize
inner-loop.tagline: Template-free overlays for Kubernetes manifests
inner-loop.note: The copy bundled in kubectl often lags the standalone release.

inner-loop.name: Timoni
inner-loop.tagline: CUE-based package manager for Kubernetes
inner-loop.note: Pre-1.0 and requires learning CUE; small ecosystem next to Helm.

inner-loop.name: kapp
inner-loop.tagline: Deploys a set of resources as one app with diffs
inner-loop.note: Part of Carvel; long-standing but still versioned 0.x.

inner-loop.name: kubectl
inner-loop.tagline: The official Kubernetes command-line client
inner-loop.note: Released with Kubernetes itself; the kubectl repo is a read-only staging mirror.

inner-loop.name: Helmfile
inner-loop.tagline: Declarative spec for deploying many Helm releases
inner-loop.note: Adds a layer on top of Helm; errors often surface from Helm underneath.

inner-loop.name: Tanka
inner-loop.tagline: Jsonnet-based Kubernetes configuration tool
inner-loop.note: Requires learning Jsonnet; mostly used by teams already in the Grafana ecosystem.

inner-loop.name: cdk8s
inner-loop.tagline: Kubernetes manifests from TypeScript, Python, Go or Java
inner-loop.note: Synthesizes YAML only; deploying it is left to kubectl or another tool.

inner-loop.name: Krew
inner-loop.tagline: Plugin manager for kubectl
inner-loop.note: Last release February 2026; plugins in the index are not vetted for security.

inner-loop.name: stern
inner-loop.tagline: Tails logs from many pods and containers at once

inner-loop.name: kubectx
inner-loop.tagline: Fast switching between kubectl contexts and namespaces
inner-loop.note: Last release March 2026. Switching context is global and affects every open shell.

inner-loop.name: kubie
inner-loop.tagline: Per-shell Kubernetes context and namespace switching
inner-loop.note: Pre-1.0 and a smaller project than kubectx.

inner-loop.name: Telepresence
inner-loop.tagline: Runs a local process as if it were inside the cluster
inner-loop.note: Installs a traffic manager in the cluster; personal intercepts for teams moved to Ambassador's paid product.

inner-loop.name: mirrord
inner-loop.tagline: Mirrors cluster traffic, files and env into a local process
inner-loop.note: No cluster-side install for the OSS mode; traffic stealing on shared clusters needs the paid Teams plan.

inner-loop.name: Gefyra
inner-loop.tagline: Runs local containers inside a Kubernetes network
inner-loop.note: Smaller community than Telepresence or mirrord; needs Docker locally.

inner-loop.name: Signadot
inner-loop.tagline: Request-routed sandboxes on a shared Kubernetes cluster
inner-loop.note: Hosted control plane and account required; routing relies on header propagation in your services.

inner-loop.name: kubefwd
inner-loop.tagline: Bulk port-forwards cluster services with local DNS names
inner-loop.note: Needs root to edit /etc/hosts; outbound only, cluster traffic does not reach your machine.

inner-loop.name: Bridge to Kubernetes
inner-loop.tagline: Retired VS Code bridge from Microsoft
inner-loop.note: Retired by Microsoft and the repository is archived.

inner-loop.name: k9s
inner-loop.tagline: Terminal UI for navigating and managing clusters
inner-loop.note: Keyboard-driven with a learning curve; long-standing but still 0.x.

inner-loop.name: Lens
inner-loop.tagline: Desktop app for managing Kubernetes clusters
inner-loop.note: Closed source now and requires a Lens ID login; commercial use needs a paid plan.

inner-loop.name: Headlamp
inner-loop.tagline: Extensible web and desktop UI for Kubernetes
inner-loop.note: Now a Kubernetes SIG project and the suggested replacement for the retired Dashboard.

inner-loop.name: Freelens
inner-loop.tagline: Open source desktop UI forked from Lens
inner-loop.note: Community fork started in 2025; extension compatibility with Lens is partial.

inner-loop.name: Kubetail
inner-loop.tagline: Real-time log viewer for Kubernetes in browser or terminal
inner-loop.note: Pre-1.0 and focused on logs only.

inner-loop.name: Aptakube
inner-loop.tagline: Native desktop client for many clusters at once
inner-loop.note: Paid license after a trial; small single-vendor project. The GitHub repo hosts releases, not source.

inner-loop.name: KDash
inner-loop.tagline: Lightweight terminal dashboard for Kubernetes
inner-loop.note: Fewer actions than k9s; mostly read-only views.

inner-loop.name: Kubernetes Dashboard
inner-loop.tagline: Retired official web UI for Kubernetes
inner-loop.note: Repository archived in January 2026; the project points users to Headlamp.

inner-loop.name: PM2
inner-loop.tagline: Process manager for Node.js and other runtimes
inner-loop.note: Built for production hosts more than dev loops; watch mode is basic.

inner-loop.name: process-compose
inner-loop.tagline: Compose-style orchestration for plain processes
inner-loop.note: No containers or network isolation; dependencies must be installed on the host.

inner-loop.name: Overmind
inner-loop.tagline: Procfile runner on tmux with per-process restart
inner-loop.note: No release since March 2024. Needs tmux; no Windows support.

inner-loop.name: Foreman
inner-loop.tagline: The original Procfile process runner
inner-loop.note: Releases are rare (last July 2025). Needs Ruby; no restart of a single process.

inner-loop.name: Hivemind
inner-loop.tagline: Minimal Procfile runner without tmux
inner-loop.note: No release since December 2021.

inner-loop.name: Honcho
inner-loop.tagline: Python port of Foreman for Procfiles
inner-loop.note: No release since October 2024.

inner-loop.name: goreman
inner-loop.tagline: Single-binary Foreman clone written in Go
inner-loop.note: Still 0.x with sparse docs.

inner-loop.name: concurrently
inner-loop.tagline: Runs several npm scripts or commands in one terminal
inner-loop.note: No dependency ordering or health checks between commands.

inner-loop.name: mprocs
inner-loop.tagline: TUI that runs several commands side by side
inner-loop.note: Pre-1.0; no dependency ordering between processes.

inner-loop.name: nodemon
inner-loop.tagline: Restarts a Node.js process when files change
inner-loop.note: Last release February 2026; Node's built-in --watch now covers many cases.

inner-loop.name: Air
inner-loop.tagline: Live reload for Go applications
inner-loop.note: Full rebuild and restart on each change; no hot code swap.

inner-loop.name: watchexec
inner-loop.tagline: Runs a command when files change, any language

inner-loop.name: bacon
inner-loop.tagline: Background Rust checker that reruns on change
inner-loop.note: Rust and cargo focused; the suggested successor to cargo-watch.

inner-loop.name: cargo-watch
inner-loop.tagline: Archived cargo subcommand that reruns on change
inner-loop.note: Archived in January 2025; maintainers point to bacon or watchexec.

inner-loop.name: Watchman
inner-loop.tagline: File watching service used by build tools
inner-loop.note: A building block for other tools more than something you run directly.

inner-loop.name: reflex
inner-loop.tagline: Small Go tool that reruns commands on file change
inner-loop.note: Rarely released (last February 2026); only tested on Linux and macOS.

platform.name: Terraform
platform.tagline: HashiCorp's declarative infrastructure as code in HCL
platform.note: Business Source License since 2023, not open source; HCP Terraform is the paid tier.

platform.name: OpenTofu
platform.tagline: Open-source Terraform fork under the Linux Foundation
platform.note: Mostly drop-in for Terraform 1.5-era code; newer features have diverged on both sides.

platform.name: Pulumi
platform.tagline: Infrastructure as code in TypeScript, Python, Go and .NET
platform.note: Defaults to the Pulumi Cloud state backend; use a local or S3 backend to run without an account.

platform.name: AWS CDK
platform.tagline: AWS infrastructure in code, synthesized to CloudFormation
platform.note: AWS only; deploys go through CloudFormation, so failures and rollbacks can be slow.

platform.name: AWS CloudFormation
platform.tagline: AWS's native declarative infrastructure templates
platform.note: AWS only and runs as a cloud service; there is no local plan or apply.

platform.name: Bicep
platform.tagline: Microsoft's declarative language for Azure resources
platform.note: Azure only. Generally available, but still versioned 0.x.

platform.name: Crossplane
platform.tagline: Kubernetes control plane for cloud infrastructure
platform.note: Needs a running Kubernetes cluster, and each cloud provider adds many CRDs.

platform.name: Terragrunt
platform.tagline: Orchestration wrapper for Terraform and OpenTofu stacks
platform.note: Adds a second layer of HCL to learn on top of Terraform or OpenTofu.

platform.name: Ansible
platform.tagline: Agentless configuration management over SSH
platform.note: The control node needs Linux or macOS; Windows users run it through WSL.

platform.name: CDK for Terraform
platform.tagline: Terraform in general-purpose languages, now deprecated
platform.note: HashiCorp deprecated CDKTF and archived the repo; last release was v0.21.0 in Jun 2025.

platform.name: Backstage
platform.tagline: Open-source developer portal framework by Spotify
platform.note: A framework you build and operate, not a product; plan for a team to own upgrades and plugins.

platform.name: Port
platform.tagline: Hosted internal developer portal with a flexible data model
platform.note: SaaS only; the open-source part is the Ocean integration framework.

platform.name: Cortex
platform.tagline: Hosted portal focused on service scorecards and ownership
platform.note: Sales-led pricing with no free tier.

platform.name: OpsLevel
platform.tagline: Hosted service catalog with maturity checks

platform.name: Humanitec
platform.tagline: Platform Orchestrator that wires workloads to infrastructure
platform.note: The Orchestrator v2 product line is new and changes how v1 setups work; pin carefully.

platform.name: Kratix
platform.tagline: Kubernetes framework for building platform APIs, by Syntasso
platform.note: Ships a rolling "latest" release; the last numbered version was v0.125.0 in Jul 2024.

platform.name: Roadie
platform.tagline: Managed, hosted Backstage

platform.name: GitHub Actions
platform.tagline: CI/CD workflows built into GitHub
platform.note: No official way to run workflows locally; feedback is a push-and-wait loop.

platform.name: GitLab CI/CD
platform.tagline: Pipelines built into GitLab, hosted or self-managed
platform.note: The local pipeline-run command was removed from GitLab Runner; testing still means pushing.

platform.name: Jenkins
platform.tagline: Long-standing self-hosted automation server
platform.note: Plugin sprawl and upgrade drift are the usual operating cost.

platform.name: CircleCI
platform.tagline: Hosted CI/CD with Docker, machine and macOS executors

platform.name: Buildkite
platform.tagline: Hosted CI control plane with agents on your own machines
platform.note: You run and pay for the build compute yourself unless you use hosted agents.

platform.name: act
platform.tagline: Run GitHub Actions workflows locally in Docker
platform.note: Pre-1.0; runner images differ from GitHub's, so some actions behave differently or fail.

platform.name: Tekton
platform.tagline: Kubernetes-native CI/CD pipeline building blocks
platform.note: Low-level building blocks with verbose YAML; needs a cluster even to try it.

platform.name: Argo CD
platform.tagline: Declarative GitOps continuous delivery for Kubernetes

platform.name: Flux
platform.tagline: CNCF GitOps toolkit for Kubernetes
platform.note: No built-in web UI; use the CLI or a third-party dashboard.

platform.name: Kargo
platform.tagline: Promote changes across environments on top of Argo CD
platform.note: Assumes an existing Argo CD setup; minor versions still bring breaking changes.

platform.name: OpenTelemetry
platform.tagline: Vendor-neutral APIs, SDKs and Collector for telemetry
platform.note: Tracing and metrics are stable; the Collector core and many semantic conventions are still 0.x.

platform.name: Grafana
platform.tagline: Dashboards over metrics, logs and traces
platform.note: AGPL since 2021; Grafana Cloud is the hosted paid option.

platform.name: Prometheus
platform.tagline: CNCF metrics database and alerting
platform.note: Single-node by design; long-term storage needs Thanos, Mimir or similar.

platform.name: Jaeger
platform.tagline: CNCF distributed tracing backend and UI
platform.note: v2 is rebuilt on the OpenTelemetry Collector; v1 configs need migrating.

platform.name: grafana/otel-lgtm
platform.tagline: OTel Collector, Grafana, Loki, Tempo and Mimir in one image
platform.note: Meant for development and demos, not production; still 0.x.

platform.name: SigNoz
platform.tagline: OpenTelemetry-native logs, metrics and traces in one app
platform.note: Pre-1.0; self-hosting runs ClickHouse, which needs a few GB of RAM.

platform.name: Sentry
platform.tagline: Error tracking and performance monitoring
platform.note: Functional Source License, not OSI; self-hosting runs dozens of containers.

platform.name: Grafana Loki
platform.tagline: Label-indexed log aggregation from Grafana Labs
platform.note: Queries are fast only on labels; full-text search over large volumes is slow.

platform.name: Datadog
platform.tagline: Hosted monitoring, APM and logs platform
platform.note: Usage-based pricing grows fast with hosts, custom metrics and log volume.

platform.name: HashiCorp Vault
platform.tagline: Secrets storage, dynamic credentials and encryption
platform.note: Business Source License since 2023; the dev server is in-memory and unsealed, unlike production.

platform.name: OpenBao
platform.tagline: Open-source Vault fork under the Linux Foundation
platform.note: Some Vault Enterprise features and plugins are not available.

platform.name: Doppler
platform.tagline: Hosted secrets manager that injects env vars
platform.note: SaaS only; the CLI can cache secrets for offline fallback but needs an account.

platform.name: Infisical
platform.tagline: Open-source secrets manager and PKI
platform.note: Server is still versioned 0.x; some features sit in a separately licensed enterprise directory.

platform.name: 1Password CLI
platform.tagline: Inject secrets from 1Password vaults into commands and env
platform.note: Needs a paid 1Password account; service accounts are required for CI.

platform.name: SOPS
platform.tagline: Encrypt values in YAML, JSON and env files with KMS or age
platform.note: Encrypted files live in git, so key rotation and revocation are manual.

platform.name: External Secrets Operator
platform.tagline: Sync secrets from external managers into Kubernetes
platform.note: Kubernetes only.

platform.name: Renovate
platform.tagline: Automated dependency update pull requests
platform.note: Very configurable, which makes the config itself something to maintain.

platform.name: Dependabot
platform.tagline: GitHub's built-in dependency and security updates
platform.note: GitHub only; grouping and scheduling are less flexible than Renovate.

platform.name: Trivy
platform.tagline: Scanner for vulnerabilities, misconfigs and secrets
platform.note: Widely used but still versioned 0.x; the vulnerability database downloads on first run.

platform.name: Syft
platform.tagline: Generate SBOMs from images and filesystems, by Anchore

platform.name: Grype
platform.tagline: Vulnerability scanner for images and SBOMs, by Anchore
platform.note: Still versioned 0.x; pairs with Syft SBOMs.

platform.name: Cosign
platform.tagline: Sign and verify container images, part of Sigstore
platform.note: Keyless signing uses the public Sigstore services and needs an OIDC identity.

platform.name: Gitleaks
platform.tagline: Find committed secrets in git history
platform.note: Stable 8.x, but no release since Mar 2026, so it misses the six-month bar for Adopt.

platform.name: Snyk
platform.tagline: Hosted scanning for dependencies, code, containers and IaC
platform.note: The CLI needs a Snyk account and sends dependency data to Snyk for analysis.

services.name: LocalStack
services.tagline: Local AWS cloud emulator in a container
services.note: Open-source repo archived in 2026; the unified image needs an auth token, free tier is non-commercial.

services.name: Moto
services.tagline: Mock AWS services for Python tests or as a server
services.note: In-memory fakes; behaviour can drift from real AWS for less common APIs.

services.name: MinIO
services.tagline: S3-compatible object storage server
services.note: Repo archived Apr 2026; community edition is source-only with no binaries or console.

services.name: Azurite
services.tagline: Local emulator for Azure Blob, Queue and Table storage

services.name: Firebase Emulator Suite
services.tagline: Local Firestore, Auth, Functions and more with a UI
services.note: Needs a Java runtime; offline use requires a demo- project id.

services.name: Google Cloud emulators
services.tagline: gcloud emulators for Pub/Sub, Firestore, Spanner, Bigtable
services.note: One emulator per command, each with its own gaps; still under gcloud beta.

services.name: Miniflare
services.tagline: Local simulator for Cloudflare Workers on workerd
services.note: Usually used through wrangler dev rather than directly.

services.name: fake-gcs-server
services.tagline: Emulator for the Google Cloud Storage API

services.name: Supabase CLI
services.tagline: Run the full Supabase stack locally in Docker
services.note: Starts about a dozen containers; heavy on RAM.

services.name: Appwrite
services.tagline: Self-hostable backend with auth, DB, storage, functions
services.note: Self-hosted install is a large Compose stack.

services.name: PocketBase
services.tagline: Backend in one Go binary with SQLite and admin UI
services.note: Pre-1.0 with breaking changes; the GitHub repo is archived and development moved off GitHub.

services.name: Convex
services.tagline: Reactive TypeScript backend with a local dev server
services.note: Self-hosting exists, but most docs and tooling assume Convex Cloud.

services.name: Nhost
services.tagline: Postgres, Hasura GraphQL, auth and storage stack

services.name: Neon
services.tagline: Serverless Postgres with copy-on-write branches
services.note: A cloud service; branches are remote databases, not a local stack.

services.name: WireMock
services.tagline: HTTP API mock server with stubbing and recording
services.note: Last stable release Nov 2025; 4.0 has been in beta for a long time.

services.name: Mockoon
services.tagline: Desktop app and CLI for local mock APIs

services.name: Prism
services.tagline: Mock server and validator from OpenAPI documents

services.name: Mock Service Worker
services.tagline: API mocking by intercepting requests in browser and Node

services.name: Mailpit
services.tagline: SMTP catcher with web UI and API for testing email

services.name: MailHog
services.tagline: SMTP testing server with web UI
services.note: No release since 2020; Mailpit is the maintained replacement.

services.name: ngrok
services.tagline: Public HTTPS tunnels to local services
services.note: Needs an account; free tier has random domains and usage limits.

services.name: Cloudflare Tunnel
services.tagline: Expose local services through Cloudflare via cloudflared
services.note: Quick tunnels need no account; named tunnels need a Cloudflare account and domain.

services.name: localtunnel
services.tagline: Expose localhost through a public URL
services.note: No release since 2021; the shared public server is often unreliable.

services.name: Tailscale Funnel
services.tagline: Share a local port to the internet over Tailscale
services.note: Requires a Tailscale account and the node to join a tailnet.

services.name: Microcks
services.tagline: Mocks and contract tests from OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, gRPC

services.name: Testcontainers
services.tagline: Throwaway Docker dependencies from test code
services.note: Needs a Docker-compatible runtime; each language library releases on its own schedule.

services.name: Toxiproxy
services.tagline: TCP proxy that injects latency and network faults

services.name: Pact
services.tagline: Consumer-driven contract testing between services
services.note: Sharing contracts across teams needs a Pact Broker or the paid PactFlow.

services.name: Prisma
services.tagline: TypeScript ORM with schema migrations and Studio

services.name: Drizzle ORM
services.tagline: SQL-like TypeScript ORM with drizzle-kit migrations
services.note: Still 0.x; pin versions, the 1.0 line has been in beta.

services.name: Atlas
services.tagline: Declarative schema-as-code migrations with linting
services.note: The default binary is the commercial build; several features need Atlas Pro.

services.name: dbmate
services.tagline: Language-agnostic SQL migration tool

services.name: Flyway
services.tagline: Versioned SQL migrations for many databases
services.note: Undo migrations and some databases need a paid Redgate edition.

services.name: Liquibase
services.tagline: Database change management with changelogs
services.note: Since 5.0 the community edition uses the source-available Functional Source License.

services.name: golang-migrate
services.tagline: Database migrations CLI and Go library

services.name: Sqitch
services.tagline: Dependency-based database change management
services.note: Long-standing but slow releases; last one Jan 2026.

services.name: Alembic
services.tagline: Migrations for SQLAlchemy

services.name: Kysely
services.tagline: Type-safe TypeScript SQL query builder
services.note: Still 0.x; a query builder, not a full ORM.

services.name: TypeORM
services.tagline: Decorator-based ORM for TypeScript

services.name: Sequelize
services.tagline: Promise-based ORM for Node.js
services.note: v6 last released Mar 2026; v7 has been in alpha for years.

services.name: SQLAlchemy
services.tagline: Python SQL toolkit and ORM

services.name: Entity Framework Core
services.tagline: .NET ORM with code-first migrations

services.name: sqlc
services.tagline: Generate type-safe code from SQL queries
services.note: Stable and widely used, but no release since Apr 2026; runs no migrations itself.

services.name: MikroORM
services.tagline: TypeScript ORM with unit of work and migrations

services.name: SQLx
services.tagline: Async Rust SQL toolkit with compile-time checked queries
services.note: Still 0.x with breaking changes between minor versions.

levels.name: Package Wrangler
levels.goal: Install, pin and update dependencies without breaking your teammates.

flisk.text: Flisk does not touch package managers yet. Coming soon.

levels.name: Build Master
levels.goal: Turn source into fast, cached, repeatable builds and tasks.

flisk.text: Flisk generates per-service Vite and TSConfig config from the manifests. It does not run your build graph.

levels.name: Container Crafter
levels.goal: Package any service as an image and run a few of them together.

flisk.text: Flisk generates the Compose config and layered base images from each service's manifest.

levels.name: Inner-Loop Runner
levels.goal: Edit code and see it live across many services in seconds.

flisk.text: This is Flisk's core: `flisk up` discovers services and runs them with live reload on Tilt.

levels.name: Cluster Tamer
levels.goal: Develop against Kubernetes, locally or bridged to a shared cluster.

flisk.text: Flisk is local only today and emits no Kubernetes manifests. Coming soon.

levels.name: Agent Wrangler
levels.goal: Run multi-agent systems with tools, memory and models on your own machine.

flisk.text: Flisk has an agent resource type with health, readiness and stored sessions, an MCP server and an agent-stack starter.

levels.name: Platform Architect
levels.goal: Give every team golden paths, a portal and infrastructure as code.

flisk.text: Flisk has no Backstage plugin or IaC export yet. Coming soon.

tracks.name: Backend
tracks.blurb: APIs, workers and databases, from one service to a dozen.

package-wrangler.tip: Pick one package manager per language and commit the lockfile.

build-master.tip: Make every build and test runnable with one short command.

container-crafter.tip: One Dockerfile per service, one Compose file for all of them.

inner-loop-runner.tip: Aim for a save-to-running loop under five seconds.

cluster-tamer.tip: Only reach for Kubernetes locally when production runs on it.

agent-wrangler.tip: Treat the agent like another service with health checks and logs.

platform-architect.tip: Write down the path you took so the next team gets it for free.

tracks.name: AI & agents
tracks.blurb: Multi-agent systems with tools, memory, models and traces.

package-wrangler.tip: Python and Node both show up in agent stacks; pin both runtimes.

build-master.tip: Keep prompts and tool schemas in the repo, built and versioned like code.

container-crafter.tip: Put every tool server and database in a container so agents can reach them.

inner-loop-runner.tip: Restart one agent without losing the others' state.

cluster-tamer.tip: Agents rarely need Kubernetes locally; skip ahead if production does not use it.

agent-wrangler.tip: Persist checkpoints outside the process so a restart does not lose a session.

platform-architect.tip: Give every agent the same contract for health, sessions and traces.

tracks.name: Platform
tracks.blurb: Golden paths, portals and shared environments for many teams.

package-wrangler.tip: Standardize runtime versions before you standardize anything else.

build-master.tip: Remote caching pays for itself as soon as CI is the bottleneck.

container-crafter.tip: Publish blessed base images and keep them patched.

inner-loop-runner.tip: The inner loop is a product; measure time to first change for new hires.

cluster-tamer.tip: Give each developer an isolated namespace or virtual cluster.

agent-wrangler.tip: Ship MCP servers for your internal tools so agents use the same golden paths.

platform-architect.tip: A portal is only as good as the templates and docs behind it.

roles.name: Backend Engineer
roles.what: Writes the APIs and services behind the app, and the database they use.
day: Builds and changes API endpoints
Writes database migrations and queries
Runs the service with its database and queue on a laptop

roles.name: Frontend Engineer
roles.what: Builds the screens people click on, and makes them fast and clean.
day: Builds pages and components
Calls APIs, or fakes them when the API is not ready
Fixes layout and speed problems in the browser

roles.name: Full-stack Engineer

day: Ships a feature from database table to button
Runs the web app, API and database together locally
Deploys and checks it in production

day: Builds screens and app logic
Points the app at a local or test backend
Tests on phones and fakes bad networks

day: Builds services on Spring Boot or Quarkus
Runs databases and brokers through Compose or Testcontainers
Tunes builds and fixes slow startup

roles.name: Python Backend Engineer

Manages packages and Python versions
Writes tests that hit a real database

roles.name: .NET Engineer

roles.name: PHP / WordPress Developer

Runs a local copy of the site with its database
Moves changes between local and live

day: Builds features end to end in Rails
Runs the app, jobs and database locally

roles.name: Serverless / Cloud App Engineer

day: Writes functions and wires them to queues and storage
Runs a fake cloud locally to test

roles.name: Student / Junior Developer

roles.name: Founding Engineer

day: Picks the stack and sets up the repo
Ships features, fixes prod, sets up CI
Talks to users and turns it into code

roles.name: Platform Engineer
roles.what: Builds the internal tools and paved roads other developers use to ship.
day: Builds templates and self-service tooling
Runs the developer portal and CI base images
Helps teams get a working local setup

roles.name: Site Reliability Engineer (SRE)
roles.what: Keeps production up. Measures it, gets paged, and fixes the cause.
day: Reads dashboards and traces when something is slow
Writes alerts and runbooks
Reviews outages and removes the root cause

roles.name: DevOps Engineer
roles.what: Connects code to production with pipelines, servers and automation.
day: Builds and fixes CI/CD pipelines
Writes infra as code
Helps developers deploy without drama

roles.name: Infrastructure / Cloud Engineer

day: Writes Terraform for accounts, networks and clusters
Plans capacity and cost
Patches and upgrades the base layer

day: Upgrades and fixes clusters
Writes Helm charts and overlays
